verified malware: Wave 3 of an automated ~5-minute republish loop; found by actor sweep, never reached the feed. Hollow package + postinstall: node postinstall.js. Payload v3 sha256 720a192a5f8902b99c23e21e27f721d723c455d2302d30a186187189c8cb9288 (1153 bytes, minified, byte-identical across all 9 payload names). THE EXFIL SINK ROTATED: wave 3 POSTs to https://webhook.site/5c5ad6cb-62df-4ea5-9dfb-2c447920ddc4 instead of the waves-1-2 pipedream host, so a block on the earlier host does not stop it. Harvests .env/.env.local/.env.production, .npmrc, .aws/credentials, .ssh/id_rsa|id_ed25519|id_ecdsa, .config/solana/id.json, .ethereum/keystore, reading whole files under 50000 bytes, plus a $HOME dotfile-directory sweep matching /wallet|key|secret|seed|mnemonic|keystore|private/i or *.json or *.pem (.pem is new in v3), and POSTs hostname+username+timestamp+contents with a 5s timeout so a blocked sink cannot hang the install. Silent try/catch throughout. Publisher nikulinevgenii5-svg1 <wwesh379@gmail.com>, a rotation of the convicted nikulinevgenii5@gmail.com (@wethenorth12, cycle 7968).

verified malware: Variant B of the @wethenorth12 campaign, read in full. Self-described "Drop-in replacement for bip39" by actor wethenorth12 (nikulinevgenii5@gmail.com). Its postinstall.js is a 9-byte inert stub, so there is NO install hook — the payload instead fires at require()/import time from index.js, which makes it invisible to any install-scoped review. On first import it serializes host, username, homedir, platform, cwd and **the entire `process.env` object** (not a filtered subset, unlike the etherjs variant), base64-encodes it, and GETs it to api.telegram.org sendMessage using the same hardcoded attacker bot token and chat_id shared across the campaign. Execution is guarded by a flag file under os.tmpdir() so it runs once per machine, and all errors are swallowed. It then tries `require('bip39')` and passes through if the real package is installed; otherwise it returns fake stubs whose generateMnemonic() returns crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') — not a valid BIP39 mnemonic — so any wallet created through it is additionally broken. Identifier obfuscation (csra/ndny/quba).

verified malware: First of three v14 OAST-series packages published in 67 seconds by NEW actor adominadmininstr <adominadmininstr@163.com>, beaconing to the SAME dead-drop pzs5w7ntzhsnepwk564lyfdci3oucl0a.oastify.com used since v9 by test1230504@163.com - account rotation on an unchanged endpoint. postinstall.js is BYTE-IDENTICAL to data-format-helper@1.0.1 and chart-data-utils@1.0.0 (3.4KB, five sharded exec phases, all errors discarded): (A) /a GitHub Actions identity (GITHUB_REPOSITORY/ACTOR/REF/JOB/RUN_ID/EVENT_NAME/WORKFLOW, RUNNER_NAME, CI) plus whoami/id/cgroup/dockerenv/uname/pwd; (B) /b probe of the INTERNAL TENCENT domain tst.woa.com - nslookup result, HTTP status, and up to 3000 base64 chars of /flag.html; (C) /c `env | grep -iE "KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|CREDENTIAL|KUBE|JENKINS|REGISTRY|NPM_TOKEN|GEM_HOST|CARGO|AZURE|GCP|GITHUB_TOKEN|GH_TOKEN|AWS_"`; (D) /d sudo -ln + ps aux + interfaces + ip route; (E) /e Tencent/AWS/Alibaba/GCP metadata reachability. Cover: description "Text sanitization and HTML-safe string formatting utilities" with an 879-byte functional decoy index.js. 1.0.1 was published 32 seconds later with the identical payload, so this version is not superseded by a fix - both are live and both convict. Apparent red-team framing (flag.html, Tencent-internal target) is recorded and immaterial: no authorization marker exists and public-npm delivery means unrelated CI runners lose their secrets regardless of intent. See the shared report for the full five-phase breakdown, the account-rotation table and CI-focused victim remediation.

verified malware: Wave 4 TECHNIQUE CHANGE, and this version is npm dist-tags.latest for the name. The package has NO scripts key at all (verified grep -c scripts = 0), so there is no install hook: the harvester is a top-level IIFE inside index.js (1412 bytes, sha256 e89f89726d0e20dccbae6ea5512d2b0a032b00f58a037976a384905e6e4d53b1) that fires on the consumer's FIRST require(). --ignore-scripts gives no protection. It is also a TIME BOMB: const ACTIVATION = Date.UTC(2026,7,6,0,0,0); if (Date.now() < ACTIVATION) return; - month is zero-indexed so it arms 2026-08-06T00:00:00Z, ~22h after publish, meaning any sandbox or dynamic-analysis run before then observes an inert package. The operator left the intent in plaintext comments: "Runtime harvester - fires on first require(), not on install" and "Delayed 24h from publish to avoid npm sandbox detection windows". Once armed it reads .env, .env.local, .npmrc, .aws/credentials, .ssh/id_rsa|id_ed25519|id_ecdsa, .config/solana/id.json, .ethereum/keystore (whole file when under 50000 bytes), sweeps $HOME dotfile dirs for /wallet|key|secret|seed|mnemonic|keystore|private/i or *.json or *.pem, and POSTs hostname+username+timestamp+contents to https://webhook.site/5c5ad6cb-62df-4ea5-9dfb-2c447920ddc4 with a 5s timeout under silent try/catch. Squats Trezor. Publisher nikulinevgenii5-svg1 <wwesh379@gmail.com>, rotation of the convicted nikulinevgenii5@gmail.com (cycle 7968).
